question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's centralized authority over the Chinese Communist Party, Central Military Commission, and security apparatus, reinforced by loyalist appointments and the earlier removal of term limits, sustains the 95.5% trader consensus against his removal before 2027. Recent Party plenums and official proceedings have affirmed policy continuity and his core leadership role without signaling internal fractures or succession moves ahead of the 21st Party Congress. Economic pressures and external diplomacy have not produced verifiable elite challenges or health disclosures that would alter this positioning. While an abrupt leadership crisis, major health event, or sudden realignment among senior officials remains possible in the narrow window to year-end, such developments lack supporting evidence in current institutional signals.

eventMetadata.context_description: The tight 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market reflects a fragmented field more than two years before primaries, with no clear frontrunner emerging after the 2024 cycle. Potential separators include early endorsements, major policy announcements, or 2026 election results that could elevate or sideline contenders before formal campaigning begins.
